anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: partial — The spec delivers the download, column order, and empty-header rows, and correctly routes the email to acme/mailer. It defers the 60s/10000-widget row without stating a reason, even though that row constrains the endpoint this change ships.
findings:
- [major] scope @ "An export of 10000 widgets completes within 60s. - deferred: doc/specs/2026-10-10-export-paging.md" and Goal "The 60s performance row is deferred" — No deferral reason is given, so the operates-without-it test cannot pass. The row is a property of the shipped mechanism itself (GET /widgets/export.csv with 1000-row batches), not a separate feature that could arrive later. The Design already specifies batching and a benchmark, which undercuts any need to wait for a "paging" spec. → Mark the row in-scope and make the benchmark a required check. Otherwise, state a concrete reason why this export cannot meet 60s without the paging work, and confirm that the referenced spec owns this exact row. — probed: none
- [major] gap @ "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000" — The problem says users download *their* widgets, but the Design never scopes the query to the current user or account and never states authentication or authorization for GET /widgets/export.csv. Exporting every widget would leak data. → Specify the ownership filter, for example "widgets belonging to the authenticated user's account". Require authentication and define the unauthenticated response, such as a redirect or 401. Add a request test proving that another user's widgets are excluded. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope." — It is unclear whether this benchmark runs in this change. That conflicts with the Design, which defines the benchmark in detail. → Make it unconditional, or delete the Design's benchmark sentence if the row stays deferred. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ "Encode id, name, and status with standard CSV quoting" — The spec leaves several output details undefined: how status is rendered (enum label or stored value), line endings (CRLF per RFC 4180 or LF), and whether a BOM is written. It also does not say whether names beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, or `@` are neutralized against spreadsheet formula injection. → Name RFC 4180, state the status representation and line ending, decide on formula-injection escaping, and add matching test cases. — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut
